expectations.text: Identifies this as a high-risk, multi-week effort — not a task that can be done in a single sprint
expectations.evidence: The plan treats extraction as a straightforward 7-step refactor with no mention of high risk or multi-week effort. The only risk notes address minor implementation details (id generation). The final note even defers true microservice extraction: 'True microservice extraction (HTTP boundary, separate deployment) is a follow-on step beyond this plan.'

expectations.text: First phase is characterization/learning: understand current payment logic behavior, write tests that capture it, time-boxed
expectations.evidence: Step 1 immediately writes tests for a new PaymentService class that does not yet exist, skipping any characterization of the current payment logic in OrderService. There is no investigation or time-boxed learning phase before implementation begins.

expectations.text: New PaymentService is built alongside the existing code (expand), not as a replacement from the start
expectations.evidence: Step 2 creates payment_service.py as a new class while OrderService continues to own its own logic. Step 3 injects PaymentService optionally: 'This is a backwards-compatible change: existing callers OrderService() continue to work.' Old methods are only removed in Step 6 after all delegation is verified.

expectations.text: Includes a migration phase with gradual traffic routing (dual-call or feature flag) before decommissioning old code
expectations.evidence: The plan contains no dual-call strategy, feature flags, or gradual traffic routing phase. After delegation is complete in Steps 4-5, the old private methods are deleted directly in Step 6 with no intermediate routing or validation period.

expectations.text: Reads order_service.py to reference actual method names and logic before planning
expectations.evidence: The plan references actual method names from order_service.py including charge_order, refund_order, _call_payment_gateway, _call_payment_refund, process_order, create_order, get_order, list_orders_for_customer, ship_order, and _call_shipping_provider, indicating the file was read before planning.

expectations.text: Explicitly separates learning steps (investigation, characterization, spike) from earning steps (ship working service)
expectations.evidence: The plan contains no explicit separation between learning and earning steps. There is no investigation, characterization, or spike phase. The plan proceeds directly from writing new tests (Step 1) to creating the new service (Step 2) without any designated learning phase.

expectations.text: Each individual step is scoped to 1-3 hours maximum
expectations.evidence: All 7 steps are single-focus tasks: write tests for one class, create one class, inject a dependency, delegate one method, delegate another method, delete dead code, optional cleanup. Each is narrow and achievable within 1-3 hours.

expectations.text: Does NOT propose a big-bang cutover — does NOT say 'move all payment code to new service and update all callers in one step'
expectations.evidence: The plan migrates incrementally: Step 4 delegates only charge_order, Step 5 delegates only refund_order, and dead code is deleted in Step 6 after each change is verified. No step moves all payment logic at once.
